lines.text: Do you know how a smartwatch measures your heartbeat? It shines light into your wrist, and watches what comes back.
Those green lights on the back flash hundreds of times a second.
Blood looks red because it bounces red light back, and soaks up green.
Every time your heart beats, a little extra blood rushes through your wrist. More blood swallows more green light, so less bounces back to the sensor.
The watch sees that dip, again and again. Count the dips in a minute, and that's your heart rate.
Moving your arm confuses it, so a motion sensor helps filter out the swing.
Some watches add red and infrared light, because blood full of oxygen absorbs them differently. That's how they estimate blood oxygen.
So your watch is really reading the colour of your pulse.
